intro: The questions below, in the order they decide the answer. Each row separates three things: what the rules already settle (with the page it was read on), what is still missing, and the specific step that would close the gap. A question marked settled still needs one fact from you; nothing here is inferred from your situation, which this guide does not know.
legend: The rules answer this. You only have to confirm a fact about yourself or your paperwork.
No official page read for this guide answers it. The affected values are left blank and published on the Flagged for Review page.

groups.title: Who you are and what the money is
groups.lead: These four decide which article applies. Getting them wrong is the difference between a documented purchase and a refusal at the counter.

items.q: Does the USD 50,000 annual total cap what you can buy?
items.known: The annual total of USD 50,000 per person per year is imposed on 个人结汇 and on 境内个人购汇 only. A 境外个人 buying foreign exchange with lawful current-account RMB income is handled by documents instead (Article 59 of the 2020 current-account guidelines, as quoted by SAFE; Article 13(1) of the 2007 implementing rules). SAFE's 2024 answer gives the annual facilitation quota to holders of a Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card.
items.unknown: The FX Regulation defines 境内个人 to include a foreigner who has continuously resided in China for one year, while the Individual FX Measures define a foreign individual by passport. Which definition your bank applies to you was not confirmed.
how: Ask the bank's 结售汇 counter, before the visit, whether its system records you as 境内个人 or 境外个人, and quote both definitions.
Check whether you hold a 外国人永久居留身份证. If you do, the facilitation quota applies and the question is closed.
If you do not hold the card, plan on the documented route (Q03) and treat the USD 50,000 figure as irrelevant to your own purchase.

items.q: What kind of money is it — salary, a house sale, an inheritance, or RMB left over from an earlier exchange?
items.known: Each has its own article. Lawful current-account income earned in China: documents including the tax voucher. RMB left over from an exchange you made: the original exchange memo, valid for 24 months from the exchange date. House-sale proceeds: passport, transfer contract and registration certificate, tax voucher. Emigrant or inheritance transfers: SAFE branch approval, with the tax certificate, under the 2004 property-transfer rules.
items.unknown: Only you know which one it is. The guide cannot classify your balance and does not try.
how: List every credit into the account and label it: salary, bonus, interest, sale, gift, or a currency exchange you made.
If any part is salary, find the matching China individual income tax record for those months.
If any part is a house sale or an inheritance, read the emigrant/inheritance route before anything else, because approval replaces the counter process.

items.q: Can you show that China tax on this income was paid?
items.known: The purchase of foreign exchange against current-account income is made at the bank on the strength of your ID and materials showing the source of the funds, expressly including the tax voucher. The bank is required to review the authenticity of the documents and their consistency with the payment.
items.unknown: No page read for this guide states what a bank will accept as sufficient proof for a given amount. Whether a tax-filing form is also demanded above USD 50,000 in a single payment is unresolved.
how: Obtain your individual income tax payment record from the China tax authority for the years the money was earned.
Take the employment contract and the pay slips that match the credits into the account.

Ask the bank in writing whether it wants the 服务贸易等项目对外支付税务备案表 for a single payment above USD 50,000; Announcement 2013 No. 40 Article 1(2) names a foreign individual's work pay, while Article 4 sends a foreign individual's own outward payment to the individual FX rules.

items.q: Will one wire of the whole amount be accepted?
items.known: For documented current-account income the rules read for this guide impose no ceiling, and the bank's commission is capped, so a single wire is the cheapest shape per dollar moved. Splitting an amount to stay under a limit is expressly prohibited.
items.unknown: A bank's own channel limit for a single outgoing wire, and whether a large amount triggers a branch review, were not verified. The cost ladder assumes one wire per amount.
how: Ask the branch for its single-transaction limit for an outward personal wire.
If it is below your amount, ask what the review process is rather than splitting the payment yourself.
Re-run the cost comparison with two wires: the fixed charges are charged twice.

groups.title: Which route, and what it costs
groups.lead: Five routes carry published prices. Two of them cannot be priced from an official page at all, and are shown as blank rather than estimated.

items.q: Bank of China, HSBC China, or another mainland bank?
items.known: Bank of China: 1‰ of the remittance amount, minimum CNY 50, maximum CNY 260 per wire, plus a CNY 150 international cable fee, plus USD 25 for full-amount delivery (USD 15 where the receiving bank holds an account with Bank of China New York). HSBC China: 0.1%, minimum CNY 100, maximum CNY 500, plus CNY 120 cable, plus CNY 200 pre-collected for a USD full-amount payment. The HSBC page also shows zero wire and cable fees for individual private-banking clients and free for the 卓越理财尊尚 tier.
items.unknown: HSBC China's own CNY/USD rate was not obtained, so no all-in total exists for that route. No official tariff was opened for ICBC, CCB, ABC or CMB, so every cost cell for those banks is blank.
how: Open your own bank's published 服务价目表 (service price list) and find the cross-border remittance line; compare the percentage, the floor and the cap with the two above.
Read the bank's own USD selling rate on the day and compare it with the Bank of China board, because the rate is worth more than the fee at large amounts.
If you bank with HSBC China, ask which tariff column your account falls in before using the HSBC figures here.

items.q: Are you eligible to use Wise from China?
items.known: Wise's own help page states the conditions for sending CNY: you are not a mainland Chinese national, you have worked in China, you have a valid China tax record showing taxes paid within the last three years, and the money goes only to another account you own. Wise returns no quote above CNY 300,000 in a single transfer.
items.unknown: Whether your own bank's app or Alipay offers the Wise route to you, and your total limit, were not verified. Quotes are dated and move with the rate.
how: Open the Wise app and start a CNY transfer; it states the fee and the amount that arrives before you confirm anything.
Have the three-year tax record ready, because eligibility turns on it.
Compare the app's quote with the Bank of China wire at the same amount on the same day; the ranking of the two changes with the amount.

items.q: Is cash — carried or withdrawn abroad — a realistic part of the answer?
items.known: Carrying USD out: up to USD 5,000 equivalent needs no permit, USD 5,000 to USD 10,000 needs a bank permit, and in principle no more than USD 10,000 equivalent may be carried out. Withdrawing abroad with a mainland card: the card fee is CNY 12 plus 1% of the amount, capped at CNY 112 per withdrawal, with CNY 10,000 per card per day and CNY 100,000 per person per calendar year.
items.unknown: The card scheme's own exchange rate and any surcharge by the foreign ATM owner were not verified. The CNY 20,000 limit on carrying renminbi across the border was seen only in an excerpt of the official page.
how: Multiply the annual withdrawal cap by the rate to see the ceiling in USD; it is small against a large balance.
Do not treat cash as a way to move a large amount: the permit threshold is a limit, and breaching the carry rules carries a fine of up to 20% of the amount.
If you will carry more than USD 10,000 into the United States, file FinCEN Form 105 on arrival.

items.q: Could you send the money as renminbi and convert outside China?
items.known: SAFE's Shanghai branch states that, under 银发〔2018〕3号 and on the three principles of knowing your customer, your business and due diligence, a bank may handle other current-account cross-border renminbi settlement for an individual.
items.unknown: Whether the receiving bank accepts an incoming personal renminbi payment, and the rate it would apply, were not verified. It does not remove the need to show the source of the funds.
how: Ask your US bank whether it accepts an incoming CNY wire to a personal account, and what it charges.
Ask the China bank whether it will send CNY rather than USD for your documented income.
Price the conversion at the receiving end before choosing this: the spread abroad is not the Bank of China board.

items.q: Does a money-transfer operator such as Western Union work for this?
items.known: Western Union's China page shows bank-account delivery as temporarily unavailable, sending through partner banks, collection in cash by the recipient, and a passport as acceptable ID.
items.unknown: Fees, limits and which passport holders or destinations are restricted were not published on the page read, so nothing is priced.
how: Ask the counter for the fee and limit for your destination before relying on this route.
Expect cash collection rather than a bank deposit, and plan how the cash is deposited and reported in the US.
Treat it as unsuitable for a large balance unless the operator confirms otherwise in writing.

groups.title: The United States side
groups.lead: The transfer itself is not what the US taxes. What you owe depends on whether the income was reported in the year it was earned.

items.q: Was the China income reported on your US returns in the year it was earned?
items.known: A US citizen is taxed on worldwide income from all sources. Foreign income is translated to dollars at the rate when it was received, paid or accrued. Tax paid to China on the same income can be taken as a credit on Form 1116, or as a deduction.
items.unknown: Your filing history. If earlier years were missed, that exposure is older and larger than anything the transfer costs, and it is a question for a US preparer before money moves.
how: Collect the US returns covering the years the money was earned.
Match each year's China salary to the amount reported as foreign earned income.
If any year is missing, get advice before the wire, because the arrival of the money does not create the liability but does attract attention.

items.q: Do the FBAR and Form 8938 thresholds apply to this account?
items.known: FBAR: file when the aggregate value of foreign financial accounts exceeds USD 10,000 at any time in the calendar year, due 15 April with an automatic extension to 15 October, filed with FinCEN and not with the return. Form 8938: for an unmarried person living in the US, more than USD 50,000 on the last day of the year or USD 75,000 at any time; the thresholds are higher for joint filers and for those living abroad.
items.unknown: The maximum non-willful penalty is published as USD 16,536 and the willful maximum as USD 165,353, but the statute's alternative measure for a willful violation was not modelled.
how: Add up every foreign account you had during the year, including this one, at its highest point.
Check the filing history for both forms separately; Form 8938 does not replace the FBAR.
If either is missing for a past year, raise it with a preparer rather than filing only the current year.

items.q: Will the exchange itself create a taxable gain in the US?
items.known: For an individual disposing of foreign currency in a personal transaction, no gain is recognised from exchange-rate movement between acquisition and disposition. The statute withholds that treatment where the gain exceeds USD 200.
items.unknown: The character of a gain above USD 200, and whether a loss on a personal conversion can be deducted, were not verified.
how: Compare the rate at which the renminbi was acquired with the rate at conversion; the difference is small at these amounts unless the money has sat for years.
Keep the acquisition rate and date, because the USD 200 test is measured on the gain, not on the amount.
Ask a preparer before reporting or deducting anything beyond that.

items.q: Is any part of this money a gift, a bequest or an inheritance?
items.known: A gift or bequest from a nonresident alien individual or a foreign estate is reported on Form 3520 when the aggregate exceeds USD 100,000 in the taxable year, due the 15th day of the fourth month after the year end.
items.unknown: Whether a particular transfer is a gift, a bequest or your own property depends on the facts, and no page read for this guide settles it.
how: Establish whose money it is before it moves: your own savings, a gift, or an estate distribution.
If it is not yours, keep the will, the estate documents or the gift records, because the reporting is by the recipient.
Read the China side of the same question: inherited money leaves China by a different route with SAFE approval.

items.q: Does the 1% remittance transfer tax apply to money coming in?
items.known: No. The IRS describes the tax as applying to remittances sent from the United States to recipients in foreign countries when the sender pays with cash, a money order, a cashier's check or a similar physical instrument. The sender is liable and the provider collects it.
items.unknown: Nothing about inbound transfers; the definition is directional. The point is recorded here because the tax is easily misapplied to the wrong direction.
how: Do not budget for this tax on an incoming wire.
If you later send money out of the US by a covered method, expect the 1% to be collected at the counter.
Read the IRS page before relying on a third-party summary, since the regulations were still proposed when it was published.

groups.title: Before you commit: price, timing and the line you must not cross
groups.lead: Two questions left, and the second is the one that turns a cheap conversion into a fine.

items.q: What does the exchange rate itself cost, separately from the fees?
items.known: On the board reading used here the bank buys USD at 666.3 and sells at 669.11 per 100. Half of that gap, measured against the selling rate, is 0.2100% one way. That margin is charged on the whole amount and dwarfs the wire fee at large amounts: it is {fx10} on USD 10,000 and {fx400} on USD 400,000, before any fixed fee.
items.unknown: The board states that the transaction rate is the one that applies, so the reading here is a reference point, not a quote. The rate moves daily.
how: Read the bank's selling rate on the day of the transfer, not the rate in the middle of the board.
Compare the same one-way margin at another bank before committing; a fraction of a percent is worth more than the fee difference.
Do the conversion once rather than twice: a round trip pays the margin twice.

items.q: Is splitting the money across people, years or accounts a way to reduce the cost?
items.known: No. Evading the limits by splitting is expressly prohibited, and so is using false documents. The penalties run to 30% of the amount, and to between 30% and 100% where the case is serious, with criminal liability where a crime is constituted. Private or disguised dealing in foreign exchange is prohibited on the same scale.
items.unknown: Nothing: the prohibition is explicit. What is unresolved is whether a factual pattern is treated as splitting, which is a question for the bank and, if it arises, a lawyer.
how: Move the money once, in one documented wire, if the bank accepts it.
Never use another person's quota or ID, and never accept funds from a third party to make up an amount.
If the bank says no, ask for the reason in writing and escalate to the branch's compliance desk instead of changing the structure.

tree.title: Which route the facts point to
tree.lead: Read down from the kind of money. The method numbers are the ones used on the Methods and Cost ladder pages.
rows: Salary or other lawful current-account income earned in China
Documented purchase with ID, source materials and the tax voucher; the bank's commission is capped, so one wire is cheapest per dollar.
The same, and you hold a Foreign Permanent Resident ID Card
The annual facilitation quota applies to you; above it you fall back to M01.
RMB left over from an exchange you made in the last 24 months
Original exchange memo plus ID; no tax voucher is mentioned for this case.
Proceeds of selling a house in mainland China
Passport, transfer contract and registration certificate, tax voucher; approval practice differs by city.
Money you are taking abroad because you have emigrated
SAFE branch approval with the tax certificate; since 2014 no instalments, no head-office filing, no notarisation.
An inheritance from a person who lived in China
SAFE branch approval at the deceased's registered domicile; Form 3520 on the US side above USD 100,000.
A modest amount, and you meet Wise's conditions
The only route here with no branch visit, but capped per transfer and only to an account you own.
No route exists. Splitting, private dealing, false documents and crypto are prohibited, and the fine scale is published.
